stimulus.text: I will be as harsh as truth, and as uncompromising as justice. On this subject, I do not wish to think, or speak, or write, with moderation. . . . I am in earnest — I will not equivocate — I will not excuse — I will not retreat a single inch — AND I WILL BE HEARD.

rationales.A: The paper’s first issue carries Garrison’s pledge to be heard on slavery, and the paper spent its life making that case.

rationales.general:
1. Start with the date and the editor: Garrison launches a paper in 1831 with a pledge about slavery.
2. Match the paper to its pledge: its pages argued for ending slavery at once.
3. Set the other causes aside: none of them is the pledge Garrison prints here.
Remember: a reform paper’s first editorial tells you its cause; read it first.
